'''Daniel Ceballos Fernández''' (born 7 August 1996) is a Spanish professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[central midfielder]] for [[La Liga]] club [[Real Betis]].

Ceballos started his career at Real Betis, where he helped them win the [[Segunda División]]. He was signed by [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] in 2017, and two years later signed for [[Premier League]] club [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] on loan. He spent two seasons at Arsenal, winning the [[FA Cup]] in 2020, before returning to Real Madrid in 2021. During his time with Madrid, he won 16 trophies, including three [[UEFA Champions League]] titles, two La Liga titles and the [[Copa del Rey]]. He left the club by mutual agreement in 2026 and re-signed for former club Real Betis.

Ceballos won his first [[Cap (association football)|cap]] for Spain in September 2018, in 6–0 home win over [[Croatia national football team|Croatia]] in the [[2018–19 UEFA Nations League|UEFA Nations League]].

==Club career==
===Real Betis===
[[File:Ceballos 15001.jpg|thumb|upright|left|Ceballos at the [[Real Betis]] training ground, 2015]]

Ceballos was born in [[Utrera]], [[Andalusia]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2018/08/ceballos-turns-22 |title=Ceballos turns 22 |publisher=Real Madrid CF |date=7 August 2018 |access-date=20 June 2020}}</ref> He joined [[Sevilla FC|Sevilla]]'s youth system in 2004 at the age of eight, but was released in 2009 due to a chronic [[bronchitis]] problem.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://sevilla.eldesmarque.com/real-betis/66971-dani-nike-la-perla-que-brilla-en-el-betis-y-dejo-escapar-el-sevilla |title='Dani Nike', la perla que brilla en el Betis y dejó escapar el Sevilla|trans-title='Dani Nike', the gem who shines in Betis and who Sevilla let slip away |publisher=El Desmarque |last=Aguado |first=Ángel |language=es |date=4 November 2014 |access-date=2 December 2014}}</ref> He subsequently played for hometown club [[CD Utrera|Utrera]], and completed his development with [[Real Betis]] after signing in 2011.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.alfinaldelapalmera.com/noticias/real-betis/dani-ceballos-las-lagrimas-de-una-madre-por-un-sueno.html |title=Dani Ceballos, las lágrimas de una madre por un sueño|trans-title=Dani Ceballos, the tears of a mother for a dream |newspaper=ABC |last=González |first=M. |language=es |date=28 April 2014 |access-date=26 May 2014}}</ref> He signed a professional contract with Betis on 22 February 2014, while still a junior.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.cuentaconlacantera.com/el-betis-ata-una-joya-con-alma-de-entrenador/ |title=El Betis ata a una joya con alma de entrenador|trans-title=Betis tie up gem with the soul of a coach |publisher=Cuenta con la Cantera |language=es |date=22 February 2014 |access-date=26 May 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141207163844/http://www.cuentaconlacantera.com/el-betis-ata-una-joya-con-alma-de-entrenador/ |archive-date=7 December 2014}}</ref>

On 26 April 2014, without even appearing for [[Real Betis B|the B team]], Ceballos played his first game with the club's main squad, coming on as a late [[Substitute (association football)|substitute]] in a 1–0 [[La Liga]] home loss against [[Real Sociedad]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.espnfc.com/en/report/372874/report.html?soccernet=true |title=Real Betis 0–1 Real Sociedad |website=ESPN FC |date=26 April 2014 |access-date=26 May 2014}}</ref> He scored his first goal on 21 December, with the first of a 2–0 home win over [[Racing de Santander|Racing Santander]] in the [[Segunda División]] championship.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.marca.com/2014/12/21/futbol/2adivision/1419167919.html |title=Merino se despide con un pleno y deja al Racing en descenso|trans-title=Merino says goodbye undefeated and leaves Racing inside the relegation zone |newspaper=Marca |language=es |date=21 December 2014 |access-date=16 February 2015}}</ref> He featured in 33 matches and scored 5 times during the [[2014–15 Segunda División]] season, as Betis returned to La Liga at the first attempt.<ref name=Champions>{{cite news |url=https://elpais.com/deportes/2015/05/25/actualidad/1432550261_534517.html |title=Las siete claves del ascenso del Betis|trans-title=The seven keys of Betis' promotion |newspaper=El País |last=Pineda |first=Rafael |language=es |date=25 May 2015 |access-date=21 August 2018}}</ref>

On 15 October 2015, after lengthy negotiations, Ceballos renewed his contract until June 2020.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.mundodeportivo.com/futbol/20151015/202223500819/el-betico-dani-ceballos-renueva-hasta-2020.html |title=El bético Dani Ceballos renueva hasta 2020|trans-title=Betis' Dani Ceballos renews until 2020 |newspaper=Mundo Deportivo |language=es |date=15 October 2015 |access-date=19 January 2016}}</ref> He scored his first goal in the Spanish top flight on 16 April 2017, with the last goal in a 2–0 home win against [[SD Eibar|Eibar]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://futbol.as.com/futbol/2017/04/16/primera/1492322153_885239.html |title=Joaquín, Adán y Ceballos salvan al Betis y también a Víctor|trans-title=Joaquín, Adán and Ceballos save Betis and Víctor too |newspaper=Diario AS |last=Espina |first=José A. |language=es |date=16 April 2017 |access-date=18 August 2017}}</ref>

===Real Madrid===
[[File:Dani Ceballos.jpg|thumb|278x278px|Ceballos playing for [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] in 2018|left]]
On 14 July 2017, Ceballos signed for La Liga club [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] on a six-year contract,<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.realmadrid.com/noticias/2017/07/comunicado-oficial-dani-ceballos |title=Comunicado oficial: Dani Ceballos|trans-title=Official announcement: Dani Ceballos |publisher=Real Madrid CF |language=es |date=14 July 2017 |access-date=14 July 2017}}</ref> for a transfer fee of around €18&nbsp;million.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.marca.com/en/football/real-madrid/2017/07/08/5960b579ca474133128b456d.html |title=Ceballos rejects Barcelona to agree six-year Real Madrid contract |newspaper=Marca |location=Spain |date=8 July 2017 |access-date=17 September 2017}}</ref> He made his debut on 16 August, replacing [[Toni Kroos]] on the 80th minute of the second leg of the [[2017 Supercopa de España]], a 2–0 home victory over [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/football/2017/08/16/real-madrid-vs-barcelona-spanish-super-cup-live-score-updates/ |title=Real Madrid 2 Barcelona 0 (5–1 on aggregate): Woeful Barca dismissed as Zinedine Zidane's unstoppable side win Super Cup |newspaper=The Daily Telegraph |last=Bull |first=JJ |date=16 August 2017 |access-date=17 August 2017}}</ref> On 23 September, in his first start, he scored two goals in a 2–1 away win over [[Deportivo Alavés|Alavés]].<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.marca.com/eventos/marcador/futbol/2017_18/la-liga/jornada_6/ala_rma/ |title=Tomen nota de Ceballos|trans-title=Take note of Ceballos |newspaper=Marca |location=Spain |last=Sánchez |first=Jesús |language=es |date=23 September 2017 |access-date=23 September 2017}}</ref>

Ceballos made four appearances during the [[2017–18 UEFA Champions League]],<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.rcnradio.com/deportes/asi-llegan-las-plantillas-de-real-madrid-y-liverpool-la-final-de-la-champions |title=Así llegan Real Madrid y Liverpool a la final de la Champions|trans-title=That is how Real Madrid and Liverpool arrive to the Champions final |publisher=RCN Radio |language=es |date=25 May 2018 |access-date=29 May 2018}}</ref> as Madrid won their third consecutive and 13th overall title in [[UEFA Champions League|the tournament]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0245-0e98d7318379-716954065574-1000--madrid-beat-liverpool-to-complete-hat-trick/ |title=Madrid beat Liverpool to complete hat-trick |publisher=UEFA |date=26 May 2018 |access-date=28 May 2018}}</ref> On 13 January 2019, after only 15 minutes on the pitch and having been constantly booed by his former club's supporters, he scored from a [[Free kick (association football)|free kick]] in the last minute of a 2–1 victory against Betis at the [[Estadio Benito Villamarín]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.20minutos.es/deportes/noticia/dani-ceballos-desgraciadamente-gol-betis-real-madrid-3535753/0/ |title=Dani Ceballos, tras marcar al Betis: "Desgraciadamente, he metido el gol"|trans-title=Dani Ceballos, after scoring to Betis: "Unfortunately, I scored the goal" |newspaper=20minutos |language=es |date=13 January 2019 |access-date=18 January 2019}}</ref>

====Loan to Arsenal====
On 25 July 2019, Ceballos joined [[Premier League]] club [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] on a season-long [[Loan (association football)|loan]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/49117667 |title=Dani Ceballos and William Saliba sign for Arsenal |website=BBC Sport |date=25 July 2019 |access-date=6 September 2020}}</ref> He made his first start for Arsenal on 17 August in a 2–1 victory over [[Burnley F.C.|Burnley]], providing two assists in a man-of-the-match performance.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2019/aug/17/arsenal-burnley-premier-league-match-report |title=Lacazette and Aubameyang give Arsenal the edge over sturdy Burnley |last=Aarons |first=Ed |date=17 August 2019 |newspaper=The Observer |access-date=17 August 2019}}</ref> On 3 October, Ceballos scored his first goal for Arsenal in a 4–0 home victory against [[Standard Liège]] in the group stage of the [[2019–20 UEFA Europa League]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.standard.co.uk/sport/football/arsenal/arsenal-vs-standard-liege-highlights-watch-europa-league-goals-martinelli-willock-ceballos-a4253781.html |title=Arsenal vs Standard Liege highlights: Watch Europa League goals – Martinelli, Willock, Ceballos |last=Doyle |first=Tom |date=3 October 2019 |newspaper=London Evening Standard |access-date=19 July 2020}}</ref> On 28 June 2020, he scored his second Arsenal goal against [[Sheffield United F.C.|Sheffield United]] in stoppage time to secure a 1–2 win in the quarter-final of the [[2019–20 FA Cup]].<ref>{{cite web |url= https://www.bbc.com/sport/av/football/53211765 |title= FA Cup: Arsenal's Dani Ceballos scores late winner against Sheffield United |website=BBC Sport |date=28 June 2020 |access-date=1 May 2021}}</ref> He played the full 90 minutes in the [[2020 FA Cup Final|final]], in which Arsenal beat Chelsea 2–1 at [[Wembley Stadium]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2020/aug/01/aubameyang-arsenal-chelsea-fa-cup-final-match-report |title=Aubameyang at the double as Arsenal turn tables on Chelsea to win FA Cup |first=David |last=Hytner |newspaper=The Guardian |location=London |date=1 August 2020 |access-date=6 September 2020}}</ref>

On 4 September 2020, Ceballos was loaned to Arsenal for another season.<ref>{{Cite web |date=20 July 2023 |title=Four players extend stay at club |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/four-players-extend-stay-club |access-date=4 June 2023 |website=Four players extend stay at club |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/54034560 |title=Dani Ceballos: Arsenal re-sign midfielder on loan for second season |website=BBC Sport |date=4 September 2020 |access-date=6 September 2020}}</ref> In one of the interviews, he stated that the manager, [[Mikel Arteta]], was the main reason why he decided to stay at Arsenal, and that since joining the club he had become a much more mature player, having improved a lot.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Ceballos – I've improved so much at Arsenal|url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/ceballos-ive-improved-so-much-arsenal |publisher=Arsenal F.C. |access-date=29 January 2021}}</ref>

====Return to Real Madrid====
Ceballos missed several months of the [[2021–22 La Liga|2021–22 season]] due to a heavy injury on his left ankle that he suffered in Spain's opening game against Egypt in the [[2020 Summer Olympics]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=10 August 2021 |title=Madrid's Ceballos has 'complete tear' in ankle |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/real-madrid/story/4451064/real-madrids-dani-ceballos-has-complete-tear-of-ankle-ligaments |access-date=21 January 2023 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref> His first appearance upon his return came on 5 January 2022 as a substitute in a 3–1 away win over [[CD Alcoyano]] in the third round of [[2021–22 Copa del Rey]].<ref>{{Cite news |title=CD Alcoyano 1–3 Real Madrid |language=en-GB |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/59888178 |access-date=21 January 2023}}</ref> On 28 May 2022, he came on as a substitute for [[Luka Modrić]] in the [[2022 UEFA Champions League final]], which saw Madrid achieve a 1–0 win over [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] to lift the title.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/match/2034586/ |title=Liverpool 0–1 Real Madrid |website=UEFA |date=28 May 2022 }}</ref>

Ceballos provided an assist and scored the winning goal in a 3–2 comeback victory in the [[2022–23 Copa del Rey]] round of 16 match against [[Villarreal CF|Villarreal]] on 19 January 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Villarreal vs. Real Madrid 2–3 |url=https://www.espn.co.uk/football/report/_/gameId/661177 |access-date=21 January 2023 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref>

On 23 June 2023, Ceballos had an agreement with Los Blancos to extend the contract until 30 June 2027.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Official Announcement: Ceballos {{!}} Real Madrid CF |url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2023/06/23/official-announcement-ceballos |access-date=23 June 2023 |website=Real Madrid C.F. |language=en}}</ref> Later that year, on 12 December, he scored his first Champions League goal, securing a 3–2 away win over [[1. FC Union Berlin|Union Berlin]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.marca.com/en/football/real-madrid/cronica/2023/12/12/6578d75222601d456a8b45ba.html |title=Real Madrid secure victory over Union Berlin through Joselu and Dani Ceballos following late drama |publisher=Marca |date=12 December 2023 }}</ref> 

On 26 June 2026, Real Madrid and Ceballos reached a mutual agreement to terminate his contract, leaving the club after nine years.<ref>{{cite web|title=Official Announcement: Ceballos|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en-US/news/club/announcements/comunicado-oficial-ceballos-26-06-2026|publisher=Real Madrid CF|date=26 June 2026|access-date=26 June 2026|archive-date=26 June 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260626202142/https://www.realmadrid.com/en-US/news/club/announcements/comunicado-oficial-ceballos-26-06-2026|url-status=live}}</ref>

=== Return to Real Betis ===
On 1 September 2026, Ceballos returned to [[La Liga]] club [[Real Betis]] on a three-year contract until 30 June 2029.<ref>{{cite press release|title=Dani Ceballos joins Real Betis Balompié|url=https://en.realbetisbalompie.es/news/latest_news/dani-ceballos-joins-real-betis-balompie-32633|publisher=Real Betis|date=2 September 2026|access-date=2 September 2026|archive-date=2 September 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260902074442/https://en.realbetisbalompie.es/news/latest_news/dani-ceballos-joins-real-betis-balompie-32633|url-status=live}}</ref>

==International career==
[[File:UEFA EURO qualifiers Sweden vs Spain 20191015 163.jpg|thumb|Ceballos playing for [[Spain national football team|Spain]] 2019|237x237px]]

On 5 November 2014, Ceballos was called up to the [[Spain national under-19 football team|Spain under-19 side]],<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.marca.com/2014/11/05/futbol/equipos/betis/1415184197.html |title=Dani Ceballos tampoco estará en el duelo del Betis en Zaragoza|trans-title=Dani Ceballos will still not be available for Betis' clash in Zaragoza |newspaper=Marca |location=Spain |last=González |first=N. |language=es |date=5 November 2014 |access-date=2 December 2014}}</ref> appearing against [[Germany national under-19 football team|Germany]], [[France national under-19 football team|France]]<ref>{{cite news |url=http://sevilla.abc.es/deportes/alfinaldelapalmera/noticias/real-betis/dani-ceballos-titular-en-el-triunfo-de-espana-sub-19.html |title=Dani Ceballos, titular en el triunfo de España sub 19 |trans-title=Dani Ceballos, starter in Spain under 19 triumph |newspaper=ABC |language=es |date=15 November 2014 |access-date=2 December 2014 |archive-date=2 December 2014 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20141202105143/http://sevilla.abc.es/deportes/alfinaldelapalmera/noticias/real-betis/dani-ceballos-titular-en-el-triunfo-de-espana-sub-19.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> and [[Greece national under-19 football team|Greece]] in a tournament played in the latter nation.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://sevilla.abc.es/deportes/alfinaldelapalmera/noticias/real-betis/dani-ceballos-participa-en-otra-victoria-de-espana-sub-19.html |title=Dani Ceballos participa en otra victoria de España sub 19 |trans-title=Dani Ceballos takes part in another Spain under 19 victory |newspaper=ABC |language=es |date=17 November 2014 |access-date=2 December 2014 |archive-date=2 December 2014 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20141202105111/http://sevilla.abc.es/deportes/alfinaldelapalmera/noticias/real-betis/dani-ceballos-participa-en-otra-victoria-de-espana-sub-19.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> He made his debut for the [[Spain national under-21 football team|under-21s]] on 26 March 2015, replacing [[Samu Castillejo]] at half-time of a 2–0 [[Exhibition game#Association football|friendly]] win over [[Norway national under-21 football team|Norway]] in [[Cartagena, Spain|Cartagena]];<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.sefutbol.com/en/report-spain-beats-norway-and-strengthens-team-2–0 |title=REPORT – Spain beats Norway and strengthens the team (2–0) |publisher=Royal Spanish Football Federation |last1=Muñoz |first1=Antonio D. |date=26 March 2015 |access-date=30 March 2015}}{{dead link|date=December 2016|bot=InternetArchiveBot|fix-attempted=yes}}</ref> four days later, in [[León, Spain|León]], he made his first start, in a 4–0 win over [[Belarus national under-21 football team|Belarus]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.goal.com/es/news/2683/selecciones-juveniles/2015/03/30/10319182/espa%C3%B1a-4-0-bielorrusia-bienvenidos-al-show-de-gerard |title=España 4–0 Bielorrusia: Bienvenidos al show de Gerard Deulofeu|trans-title=Spain 4–0 Belarus: Welcome to the Gerard Deulofeu show |website=[[Goal (website)|Goal.com]] |publisher=Perform Group |language=es |date=30 March 2015 |access-date=30 March 2015}}</ref>

Despite beginning the competition in Poland on the bench, Ceballos' performances at the [[2017 UEFA European Under-21 Championship]] led Spain to the second place. Subsequently, he was named the [[2017 UEFA European Under-21 Championship#Player of the tournament|player of the tournament]].<ref name=":0">{{cite web |url=https://www.uefa.com/under21/news/0257-0dee39848e21-bc7abea6d4a2-1000--spain-s-dani-ceballos-named-player-of-the-tournament/ |title=Spain's Dani Ceballos named Player of the Tournament |publisher=UEFA |date=30 June 2017 |access-date=30 June 2017}}</ref> With the under-21 side he also took part in the victorious [[2019 UEFA European Under-21 Championship]] Spain team. He was named in the team of the tournament for the second successive tournament.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.uefa.com/under21/news/0257-0debfa089f1b-b6025bf8b1b3-1000--official-under-21-team-of-the-tournament/ |title=Official Under-21 Team of the Tournament |publisher=UEFA |date=1 July 2019 |access-date=1 April 2020}}</ref>

Ceballos won his first [[Cap (association football)|cap]] for [[Spain national football team|the senior team]] on 11 September 2018, playing the entire 6–0 home win over [[Croatia national football team|Croatia]] in the [[2018–19 UEFA Nations League]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://en.as.com/en/2018/09/11/football/1536687949_030758.html?omnaut=1 |title=Spain – Croatia match report: UEFA Nations League |newspaper=Diario AS |last=Dunne |first=Robbie |date=11 September 2018 |access-date=11 September 2018 |archive-date=12 September 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180912022014/https://en.as.com/en/2018/09/11/football/1536687949_030758.html?omnaut=1 |url-status=dead }}</ref> He scored his first goal for his country on 15 November, in a 3–2 loss in [[Zagreb]] against the same opponent and in the same competition.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://pt.uefa.com/uefanationsleague/match/2024039--croatia-vs-spain/ |title=Croatia 3–2 Spain |publisher=UEFA |date=15 November 2018 |access-date=15 November 2018}}</ref>

On 29 June 2021, Ceballos was included as one of three overaged players in [[Spain national under-23 football team|Spain]]'s preliminary squad for the [[Football at the 2020 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2020 Summer Olympics]] after having missed out on [[UEFA Euro 2020|Euro 2020]] due to injury.<ref>{{Cite magazine|agency=Associated Press|title=Spain Names Six From Euro Squad to Olympic Roster|url=https://www.si.com/soccer/2021/06/29/spain-olympics-squad-euro-2020-pedri-dani-olmo|access-date=1 July 2021|magazine=Sports Illustrated|date=29 June 2021 |language=en-us}}</ref> In July 2021, he was included in the 22-player squad of the [[Spain national under-23 football team|under-23 team]] for the [[Football at the 2020 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2020 Summer Olympics]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Estos son los internacionales que representarán a España en Tokio |date=29 June 2021 |url=https://www.sefutbol.com/oficial-estos-son-internacionales-que-representaran-espana-tokio |publisher=SEFutbol |access-date=29 June 2021 |language=es |archive-date=4 July 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210704000851/https://www.sefutbol.com/oficial-estos-son-internacionales-que-representaran-espana-tokio |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Personal life==
Since 2023, Ceballos has been in a relationship with Luna Serrat, granddaughter of singer [[Joan Manuel Serrat]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.semana.es/corazon/luna-serrat-nieta-joan-manuel-serrat-tras-anunciar-que-espera-gemelos-no-sabeis-ganas-que-tenia-dejar-guardar-secreto_2811775 |title=La familia de Dani Ceballos y Luna Serrat opinan sobre su embarazo "por partida doble": "Nos habéis hecho tan felices" |date=9 March 2026 |access-date=11 March 2026 |newspaper=Semana |language=es}}</ref>
